name: MariaDB
tagline: Community-led MySQL fork with extra storage engines, built-in Galera and a faster feature cadence.
description: MariaDB started in 2009 as a fork of MySQL by its original authors and has since diverged into its own database with system-versioned tables, sequences, Oracle-compatibility mode, a vector type and pluggable engines such as ColumnStore and Spider. It is the default MySQL-family server on many Linux distributions and remains largely drop-in for MySQL 5.7-era applications, though newer MySQL features (and replication from MySQL 8+) are not always compatible. The server is governed by the MariaDB Foundation, while MariaDB plc, taken private by K1 Investment Management in 2024 and owner of Galera since 2025, sells the Enterprise Platform and SkySQL-style cloud offerings. Releases now follow yearly LTS plus rolling quarterly releases.

pricing.notes: Community Server is GPLv2; MariaDB Enterprise Platform (MaxScale, enterprise server, support) is a subscription.

scale.notes: Primary-replica or Galera multi-primary for HA; Spider engine and MaxScale provide sharding and routing.

strengths: System-versioned (temporal) tables for point-in-time queries in plain SQL
Native VECTOR type with HNSW indexes since 11.7, no extension needed
Galera synchronous multi-primary replication bundled in the server
Pluggable engines: ColumnStore for analytics, Spider for sharding, S3 for archives
Open development with Foundation governance and GPL code
weaknesses: Diverging from MySQL 8+/9: GTIDs, JSON storage and some syntax are incompatible
Smaller managed-service footprint than MySQL or PostgreSQL (no Cloud SQL or Azure flexible server)
Rolling releases get short support windows; production should track LTS
Corporate side has been through financial turmoil and an ownership change
useCases: Drop-in replacement for legacy MySQL deployments
Linux distribution default database for LAMP stacks
Combining relational data with vector similarity search
notIdealFor: Apps depending on the newest MySQL 8.4/9.x-only features
Large-scale analytics compared with dedicated warehouses
Teams wanting a managed service on every cloud
